scenario: 面试官只说了一句“设计一个 ML 系统”，45 分钟内你要展示解决问题的能力。
scenario_en: The interviewer only says, "design an ML system," and you have 45 minutes to show structured problem solving.
q: 为什么要按 framing→data→model→eval→deep dive 顺序推进，而不是先讲模型架构？
q_en: Why follow framing, data, model, evaluation, and deep dives instead of starting with model architecture?
options: 先定业务/ML 目标和数据，模型选择才有依据
顺序不重要，先秀模型架构的具体细节更容易拿分
应该跳过数据讨论，先调超参数再看效果
应该把全部时间都投入到一个深挖话题上
options_en: Nail the objective and data first so model choices are grounded.
Order does not matter; showing off specific architecture detail first earns more credit.
Skip the data discussion and start tuning hyperparameters before looking at any data.
Pour all 45 minutes into a single deep-dive topic instead.
why: 模型选择依赖数据和目标先确定，倒着讲会让评审觉得你在猜测而不是推导。
why_en: Framing and data must come before modeling because model choices should be derived from the objective, not guessed first.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Frame[Frame] --> Data[Data]
  Data --> Model[Model]
  Model --> Eval[Eval]
  Eval --> DeepDive[Deep dive]

termDefinitions.meaning: 面试后段针对某个具体技术难点做的深入讨论环节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A deep dive is the later interview segment focused on one specific hard part of the design.

optionExplanations: 对：目标和数据先定，模型选择才有依据，不是拍脑袋。
顺序不重要是误解——没先定目标和数据，架构细节讲再细也是空中楼阁。
跳过数据直接调参是误解——不知道数据长什么样，参数根本无从谈起。
把时间全押一个话题是误解——45 分钟要走完整个框架，不能只讲一点。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: nail the objective and data first so model choices are grounded, not guessed.
Order not mattering is the misconception — without objective and data, architecture detail is noise.
Skipping data to tune first is a misconception — you can't tune what isn't characterized yet.
Spending it all on one deep dive is the misconception — 45 minutes needs the whole framework.

scenario: 面试题是“设计电商推荐系统”，没有给候选池规模、展示位置、延迟这些约束。
scenario_en: The prompt is "design an e-commerce recommender," but candidate pool size, placement, and latency are not specified.
q: 开场该先做什么，才不会设计错方向？
q_en: What should you do first so you do not design in the wrong direction?
options: 直接开始画 Transformer 架构图
问清候选池规模、展示位置和延迟要求
只承诺“我们用 Redis 做缓存”
拒绝做任何假设，等面试官喂条件
options_en: Jump straight into drawing a Transformer architecture.
Ask about candidate pool size, placement, and latency requirements.
Commit only to "we'll use Redis for caching."
Refuse to make any assumption and wait to be spoon-fed constraints.
why: 候选池规模和展示位置决定召回和 serving 架构；没澄清就容易设计错问题。
why_en: Targeted clarification questions define the actual ML problem and prevent solving the wrong scope.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官说“你自己假设”，就明确列出假设并继续推进。
tradeoff: 澄清关键约束 vs 假设默认值快速推进

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种基于自注意力机制的神经网络架构，常用于序列建模。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Transformer is a neural network architecture built on self-attention, commonly used for sequence modeling.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用的内存型缓存/键值存储服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory key-value store commonly used as a cache.

optionExplanations: 直接画架构图是误解——规模和延迟都没问，选型全靠猜。
对：候选池规模、位置、延迟问清楚，后面设计才有依据。
只承诺用 Redis 是误解——过早锁死技术，没解决召回和延迟的真问题。
完全不做假设是误解——面试时间有限，该问的问完就该往前推进。
optionExplanations_en: Jumping to architecture is the misconception — scale and latency are unknown, so it's a guess.
Correct: ask about pool size, placement, and latency first — everything else builds on that.
Committing only to Redis is a misconception — it locks in tech before the real problem is clear.
Refusing to assume anything is the misconception — ask what you need, then keep moving.

scenario: 某内容审核系统的 KPI 是“减少违规曝光”，训练时模型只优化一个分类 loss。
scenario_en: A content moderation system's KPI is reducing harmful exposure, but training only optimizes a classification loss.
q: 业务目标和 ML loss 之间是什么关系？
q_en: How should you relate the business objective to the ML loss?
options: 两者永远完全等价，不需要区分
业务目标只是写给产品经理看的文档，训练时可以不管
业务目标是最终价值，ML loss 只是训练用的代理指标
ML loss 的取值高低不会反过来影响任何业务结果
options_en: The two are always exactly equivalent, no distinction needed.
The business objective is just paperwork for product managers and can be ignored while training.
The business objective is the real value; ML loss is only a training proxy.
The ML loss value never feeds back into any business outcome at all.
why: 真实系统优化的是留存、收入或风险，loss 只是训练模型的近似目标。
why_en: The business objective is the real value to optimize, while the ML loss is only a training proxy.
tradeoff: 业务目标（留存/收入/风险） vs ML loss（训练可优化的近似指标）

termDefinitions.meaning: 训练时用来衡量模型预测与目标差距、并据此更新参数的函数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A loss function measures how far predictions are from the target and drives parameter updates during training.

optionExplanations: 两者永远等价是误解——loss 达标不代表业务目标真的达成。
业务目标只给 PM 看是误解——目标定不好，建模方向从一开始就偏了。
对：留存、收入、风险才是真正要保的，loss 只是训练阶段能优化的近似目标。
loss 不影响业务是误解——模型学出的行为最终会体现在业务结果里。
optionExplanations_en: Assuming full equivalence is a misconception — a lower loss doesn't guarantee the goal is met.
Treating it as PM paperwork is a misconception — a bad goal misdirects modeling from day one.
Correct: retention, revenue, risk are the real prize; loss is just what training can optimize.
Assuming loss never feeds back is a misconception — learned behavior shows up in the results.

scenario: 有害内容系统把“删除内容总量最大化”定为唯一业务目标。
scenario_en: A harmful-content system defines its only business goal as maximizing the total number of removed items.
q: 这个目标设计有什么问题？
q_en: What is wrong with this objective design?
options: 会自动把误删率降到零，无需人工复核
会自动提升用户满意度，不看留存变化
会让人工审核彻底退出这套判定流程
会鼓励过度删除，伤害合法用户和表达自由
options_en: It automatically drives false positives to zero, no review needed.
It automatically raises satisfaction, regardless of retention.
It removes human review from the moderation loop entirely.
It rewards over-removal and harms legitimate users' expression.
why: 只追求删除量会忽略误删成本，和用户表达自由、留存相冲突。
why_en: Maximizing removals alone creates perverse incentives by ignoring false positives and legitimate-user harm.
whenOtherWins: 若内容明确非法且已人工确认，删除量可作为执行指标，而非唯一目标。
tradeoff: 删除量（执行效率） vs 误删代价（合法用户体验）

termDefinitions.meaning: 把合法内容错误地判成违规并处理掉。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A false positive is legitimate content that gets wrongly flagged and removed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给主指标设的约束线，防止优化走向极端。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A guardrail is a constraint metric that stops optimization from swinging to an extreme.

optionExplanations: 误删率自动降零是误解——只奖励删除量反而会推高误删。
满意度自动提升是误解——过度删除伤的正是合法用户的体验。
人工审核会消失是误解——疑难案例仍要人工兜底。
对：只看删除总量会激励系统宁可错杀，牺牲合法用户和表达自由。
optionExplanations_en: Assuming false positives drop to zero is a misconception — rewarding volume pushes them up.
Assuming satisfaction auto-improves is a misconception — over-removal hurts legit users.
Assuming human review disappears is a misconception — hard cases still need a human fallback.
Correct: rewarding removal volume alone encourages over-removal and hurts free expression.

scenario: 业务目标已经定为“提高电商转化率”。
scenario_en: The business goal has been set as improving e-commerce conversion rate.
q: 接下来要把业务目标转化成什么？
q_en: What should you translate the business goal into next?
options: 转成具体建模任务（分类/排序/回归）和技术指标
先决定最终产品界面上的 UI 文案措辞细节
提前锁定要用的云厂商和具体部署区域方案
先把所有数据库表结构和相关 SQL 语句写完
options_en: Translate it into a concrete task (classification/ranking/regression) and technical metrics.
Decide the exact wording of the final product's UI copy first.
Lock in the specific cloud vendor and deployment region ahead of time.
Finish writing every database table and its related SQL statements first.
why: ML objective 设定后，数据、模型和评估才有共同方向。
why_en: The ML objective translates the business goal into a concrete modeling task and technical success criteria.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给候选集打分并排出先后顺序的建模任务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Ranking is a modeling task that scores and orders a set of candidates.

optionExplanations: 对：要落到具体任务类型（分类/排序/回归）和可评估指标上。
直接定 UI 文案是误解——那是产品体验阶段的事，不是这一步。
锁定云厂商和区域是误解——部署选型该等约束明确后再谈。
写完所有 SQL 是误解——实现细节要等数据形态和任务定了才展开。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: land on a concrete task type — classification, ranking, regression — with metrics.
Deciding UI copy is a misconception — that's product experience, not this translation step.
Locking the cloud vendor is a misconception — deployment waits until constraints are known.
Finishing all the SQL is a misconception — implementation waits on data shape and task type.

scenario: 推荐系统目标是给用户排出 up-next 视频列表。
scenario_en: The recommender's goal is to produce an ordered up-next video list for each user.
q: ML objective 更适合定义成什么？
q_en: What is the right ML objective for this recommender?
options: 判断用户账号是否存在的二分类
给定用户和上下文，对候选视频排序
压缩视频文件体积
检测数据库死锁
options_en: A binary classifier for whether a user account exists.
Rank candidate videos given the user and session context.
Compress the video file size.
Detect database deadlocks.
why: 推荐的核心输出是有序列表，不是单条绝对判断。
why_en: Video recommendation is primarily a ranking task over candidates given user and session context.
whenOtherWins: 如果业务只问“这条内容是否违规”，二分类目标更合适。
tradeoff: 排序候选集（ranking） vs 单条绝对判断（分类）

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户当前这次访问中的行为和状态信息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Session context is the user's behavior and state during the current visit.

optionExplanations: 账号是否存在是误解——那是身份校验，产不出有序列表。
对：输出是一份 up-next 有序列表，核心目标就是给候选排序。
压缩视频体积是误解——那解决的是存储成本，不是推荐目标。
检测数据库死锁是误解——那是运维问题，跟排序无关。
optionExplanations_en: Framing it as account-existence is a misconception — that's auth, not an ordered list.
Correct: the output is an ordered list, so the objective is ranking candidates.
Framing it as compression is a misconception — that's storage cost, not recommendation.
Framing it as deadlock detection is a misconception — that's ops, unrelated to ranking.

scenario: 你要为一个内容审核系统给出高层设计。
scenario_en: You need to present the high-level design for a content moderation system.
q: High-level Design 阶段的目标是什么？
q_en: What is the goal of the high-level design stage?
options: 完整实现每个微服务的全部具体业务代码
深挖每一张表所有数据库索引的具体设计
用简单框图/描述对齐输入、组件、输出和动作
跳过高层讨论，直接进入模型训练的具体细节
options_en: Fully implement every microservice's complete business logic code.
Deep-dive into every table's database index design in detail.
Use a simple block diagram or description to align input, components, output, and action.
Skip the high-level discussion and jump straight into model-training details.
why: 高层设计是沟通支架，不是最终架构图考试。
why_en: The high-level design aligns the interviewer on inputs, components, outputs, and actions before deeper modeling.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  User[User context] --> Candidate[Candidates]
  Candidate --> Ranker[ML ranker]
  Ranker --> Action[Product action]
  Action --> Logs[Feedback logs]

termDefinitions.meaning: 用方框和箭头简要表示系统组件与数据流向的示意图。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A block diagram sketches a system's components and data flow using boxes and arrows.

optionExplanations: 完整实现每个微服务是误解——那是实现轮的活，会占掉建模时间。
深挖全部索引设计是误解——偏离了应用型 ML 面试的重点。
对：一张简单框图把输入、组件、输出、动作对齐清楚就够了。
跳过高层设计直接建模是误解——后面讨论会失去共同的系统边界。
optionExplanations_en: Fully implementing every service is a misconception — that's implementation work, not HLD.
Deep-diving every index is a misconception — it drifts from the applied ML focus.
Correct: a simple diagram aligning input, components, output, and action is enough.
Skipping this to model right away is a misconception — later discussion loses shared ground.

scenario: Applied ML 面试里你想深入讲数据库分片和 API 网关的细节。
scenario_en: In an applied ML interview, you are tempted to spend time on database sharding and API gateway details.
q: 这类 SWE 基础设施细节通常该怎么处理？
q_en: How should you handle these SWE infrastructure details?
options: 把大部分时间都花在数据库分片设计上
完全不讨论系统最终采取的动作
拒绝画出任何组件之间的框图
只在涉及 ML 推理时简要提及
options_en: Spend most of the time on database sharding design.
Never discuss the action the system ultimately takes.
Refuse to sketch any diagram of how components connect.
Mention it briefly only when it touches ML inference.
why: 应用型 ML 重点是数据、模型、评估；SWE 细节除非影响特征/推理，否则不该主导。
why_en: In an applied ML design, software infrastructure details should support the data, modeling, and evaluation story rather than dominate the interview.
whenOtherWins: 若面试明确是 ML infra 设计，服务架构和资源管理会成为主线。
tradeoff: ML 建模深度 vs SWE 基础设施细节（分片/网关）

termDefinitions.meaning: 把数据水平拆分到多台数据库实例上以提升容量和吞吐。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sharding splits data horizontally across multiple database instances to increase capacity and throughput.

termDefinitions.meaning: 统一入口，负责路由、鉴权等跨服务的请求处理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API gateway is a unified entry point that handles routing, auth, and other cross-service request concerns.

optionExplanations: 把大部分时间给分片是误解——会挤掉数据、模型、评估的时间。
完全不谈系统动作是误解——动作决定业务效果，链路里必须出现。
拒绝画框图是误解——一张框图能让面试官确认你们谈的是同一个系统。
对：SWE 细节只有牵动特征、推理或评估时才带一句，不喧宾夺主。
optionExplanations_en: Spending most time on sharding is a misconception — it crowds out time for data, modeling, and evaluation.
Never discussing the final action is a misconception — it determines business impact.
Refusing to sketch a diagram is a misconception — it keeps both sides on the same page.
Correct: mention SWE details only when they touch features, inference, or offline evaluation.

scenario: 你要为电商推荐系统准备训练数据。
scenario_en: You are preparing training data for an e-commerce recommender.
q: Data and Features 部分应该先讨论什么？
q_en: What should the Data and Features section start with?
options: 训练数据来源、标签/代理信号，及其偏差和质量
先讨论最终产品界面上按钮的颜色方案
先定好模型 checkpoint 文件的命名和版本规则
先套用生产事故发生后要用的复盘文档模板
options_en: Training data sources, labels or proxy signals, and their biases and quality.
Start with the final product's on-screen button color scheme.
Nail down the naming and versioning convention for model checkpoint files first.
Start by adopting the postmortem template used after a production incident.
why: 训练数据决定模型能学到什么，标签成本和偏差要先摸清楚。
why_en: The data section should begin with training data sources, labels or proxies, and their biases and quality.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用点击、举报等间接行为代替直接人工标签。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A proxy label uses an indirect signal like clicks or reports in place of a direct human label.

optionExplanations: 对：先把数据来源、标签或代理信号，以及偏差和质量摸清楚。
先谈按钮颜色是误解——那是产品 UI 话题，跟数据质量无关。
先谈 checkpoint 命名是误解——那是工程规范，不回答数据问题。
先谈事故复盘模板是误解——那属于运维流程，不是数据阶段该谈的。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: nail the data's origin, its labels or proxy signal, and where it's biased or noisy.
Starting with button color is a misconception — that's UI, unrelated to data quality.
Starting with checkpoint naming is a misconception — that's convention, not data quality.
Starting with a postmortem template is a misconception — that's operations, not data.

scenario: 你正在盘点电商推荐系统能用上的训练数据。
scenario_en: You are inventorying training data sources for an e-commerce recommender.
q: 训练数据可以按哪些类别组织？（多选）
q_en: Which buckets can training data be organized into? (Select all that apply.)
options: 监督数据
半监督/代理标签数据
无监督/自监督数据
前端 CSS 类名
options_en: Supervised data
Semi-supervised / proxy-label data
Unsupervised / self-supervised data
Frontend CSS class names
why: 好方案会利用少量高质量标签和大量弱/未标注数据，不同数据桶承担不同角色。
why_en: Training data can be organized into supervised, semi-supervised proxy, and unsupervised or self-supervised sources.

termDefinitions.meaning: 利用数据自身结构生成监督信号，无需人工标注。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Self-supervised learning derives its own training signal from the structure of the data without human labels.

optionExplanations: 监督数据有明确人工标签，最可靠但成本高、覆盖有限。
代理标签成本低、覆盖广，补足人工标注够不到的长尾，但要防偏差。
无监督/自监督数据不需要标签，能从海量数据学出通用表示，撑冷启动。
前端 CSS 类名不是训练信号，跟数据桶分类无关。
optionExplanations_en: Supervised data has explicit human labels — most reliable, but costly and limited in reach.
Proxy labels like clicks are cheap and broad — they cover the long tail, but carry bias risk.
Unsupervised/self-supervised data needs no labels — it helps most with cold start.
Frontend CSS class names aren't a training signal — irrelevant here.

scenario: features 阶段你已经想到 50 个候选字段。
scenario_en: During the feature discussion, you have thought of 50 possible fields.
q: 更好的表达方式是什么？
q_en: What is the better way to present the feature discussion?
options: 把 50 个候选字段逐字逐条念完，不做取舍
挑高价值信号来源，说明假设和表示方式
只强调“字段越多越好”，不解释假设
完全不谈任何字段该如何编码给模型用
options_en: Read out all 50 candidate fields one by one without prioritizing any.
Pick high-value signal sources and explain the hypothesis and representation.
Just insist "more fields is always better" without explaining the hypothesis.
Never discuss how any of the fields get encoded for the model.
why: 面试官看的是你如何判断信号价值和落地成本，而不是字段数量。
why_en: A feature discussion should prioritize high-value signal sources and representation choices instead of dumping every possible field.
whenOtherWins: 若面试官明确要求先 brainstorm 全部字段，可以先发散再收敛。
tradeoff: 少量高价值信号 + 假设 vs 穷举字段列表
optionExplanations: 逐条念完 50 个字段是误解——占时间却看不出判断力。
对：挑高价值信号，讲清假设和表示方式，面试官看的是取舍逻辑。
只说字段越多越好是误解——看不出你筛选信号价值的能力。
完全不谈编码方式是误解——模型拿不到可用的输入格式。
optionExplanations_en: Reading out all 50 fields is a misconception — it burns time without showing judgment.
Correct: pick high-value signals and explain the hypothesis behind each — that shows judgment.
Saying more fields is always better is a misconception — it hides your prioritization.
Never discussing encoding is a misconception — the model can't consume raw features.

scenario: 你已经列出类别、文本、图片、数值等候选特征。
scenario_en: You have listed candidate features such as categories, text, images, and numeric values.
q: 除了列出信号，还必须说明什么？
q_en: Beyond listing signals, what else must you explain?
options: 只报出每个变量的名称，不说别的
只说明它最终存进哪一张数据库表
每种信号如何编码/表示给模型使用
只关心模型训练跑起来的速度快慢
options_en: Just name each variable and stop there.
Just state which database table each one lives in.
How each signal is encoded or represented for the model.
Just care about how fast training runs.
why: 类别、文本、图片、数值的表示方式不同，高级回答会说明编码选择。
why_en: Feature discussion must include how each signal is represented for the model.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把类别或文本等离散信号映射成稠密向量的表示方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An embedding maps a discrete signal such as a category or text into a dense vector representation.

optionExplanations: 只报变量名是误解——名字只帮沟通，模型吃不进字符串标签。
只说存进哪张表是误解——存储位置不决定模型能不能用它。
对：无论是类别、图片还是文本、数值，都要交代编码方式，模型才吃得进去。
只关心训练速度是误解——表示方式没定好，谈速度太早。
optionExplanations_en: Naming variables only is a misconception — a name helps talk, not what the model consumes.
Naming the storage table is a misconception — location doesn't make a feature usable.
Correct: explain how each type — category, text, image, numeric — gets encoded for the model.
Focusing on speed alone is a misconception — it's premature without a representation.

scenario: 你要给推荐系统的排序模型选出第一个可运行版本。
scenario_en: You need to choose the first runnable ranking model for a recommender.
q: 为什么要先讲 benchmark/baseline？
q_en: Why should you discuss a benchmark or baseline first?
options: baseline 一定会最终上线
baseline 不需要任何数据
有了 baseline 就可以跳过评估
给复杂模型一把尺子，证明额外复杂度值得
options_en: The baseline will always ship to production.
A baseline needs no data at all.
Once you have a baseline you can skip evaluation.
It gives complex models a yardstick that justifies the extra complexity.
why: 简单 baseline 快、可解释，能判断复杂模型是否值得。
why_en: A baseline grounds the modeling discussion and gives a yardstick for justifying additional complexity.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Baseline[Simple baseline] --> Compare[Measure lift]
  Compare --> Complex[Complex model]
  Complex --> Justify[Justify cost]

termDefinitions.meaning: 用来比较后续复杂方案收益的简单参照模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A baseline is a simple reference model used to measure the gain from a more complex approach.

optionExplanations: baseline 一定上线是误解——它更常是比较用的地板线。
baseline 不需要数据是误解——没数据只能靠启发式规则。
有 baseline 就能跳过评估是误解——复杂模型的收益仍要靠评估证明。
对：baseline 设了一把尺子，让额外复杂度是否值得有据可查。
optionExplanations_en: Assuming the baseline always ships is a misconception — it's usually just a floor.
Assuming a baseline needs no data is a misconception — without data you only get heuristics.
Assuming a baseline skips evaluation is a misconception — proving any gain still needs it.
Correct: a baseline sets the yardstick complex models must beat to justify their cost.

scenario: 欺诈检测第一版有结构化数值和类别特征，延迟敏感。
scenario_en: The first fraud detection version has structured numeric and categorical features and is latency-sensitive.
q: 合理的 baseline 是什么？
q_en: What is a reasonable baseline model?
options: 轻量表格模型：LR 或 GBDT
参数量最大、延迟也最高的多模态 LLM
不看任何特征，对候选做纯随机排序
为每一个用户手写一套判断规则
options_en: A lightweight tabular model: logistic regression or GBDT.
The largest, highest-latency multimodal LLM available.
Ignore all features and score candidates with pure random ordering.
Hand-write a separate rule set for every single user.
why: 结构化 tabular 特征上，轻量模型快且有竞争力。
why_en: For structured low-latency fraud features, logistic regression or GBDT is a practical baseline.
whenOtherWins: 若输入主要是长文本或图像语义，预训练 encoder 会更有优势。
tradeoff: 轻量表格模型快速迭代 vs 大模型的语义能力

termDefinitions.meaning: 梯度提升决策树，一种在表格数据上常用且训练快的模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GBDT, gradient boosted decision trees, is a model family that trains quickly and works well on tabular data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种输出概率的线性分类模型，可解释性强。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Logistic regression is a linear classifier that outputs probabilities and is easy to interpret.

optionExplanations: 结构化特征、延迟敏感时，LR 或 GBDT 训练快、serving 便宜，是最实际的起点。
大模型适合长文本或图像语义为主、延迟宽松的场景，这里结构化又延迟紧，代价太高。
纯随机排序没有可学习信号，只能当 sanity check，不是真的 baseline。
人工规则适合少量清晰模式，覆盖不了欺诈场景持续变化的长尾。
optionExplanations_en: With structured, latency-sensitive features, LR or GBDT trains fast and serves cheap.
A giant model fits text/image inputs with loose latency — here it's structured and tight.
Random ranking carries no signal — it's a sanity check, not a real baseline.
Hand-written rules fit a few clear patterns, not fraud's shifting long tail.

scenario: 你要在结构化特征上比较“经典模型”和“深度学习模型”两条路线。
scenario_en: You need to compare classic models and deep learning models on structured features.
q: Model Selection 讨论应该覆盖哪些维度？
q_en: Which dimensions should the model selection discussion cover?
options: 只报出最新一篇论文的名字，不谈是否适配
比较模型家族的质量成本延迟权衡
只说一句“用深度学习就行”，不给理由
只讨论这套系统的数据库该选哪种类型
options_en: Just name-drop the newest paper without saying whether it fits.
Compare model families on quality, cost, and latency trade-offs.
Just say "use deep learning" and stop there, with no justification.
Just discuss which type of database this system should pick.
why: 面试官要看你能在约束下选模型，而不是盲目追求复杂。
why_en: Model selection should compare families on quality, cost, latency, interpretability, and operational complexity.
tradeoff: 质量/复杂度 vs 成本/延迟/可解释性

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户塔和物品塔分别编码，再计算相似度的推荐模型架构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A two-tower model encodes users and items in separate towers and scores them by similarity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在向量空间快速查找最相似候选的近似算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ANN, approximate nearest neighbor search, quickly finds the most similar candidates in vector space.

optionExplanations: 只报论文名是误解——新方法只有匹配约束和数据形态才有说服力。
对：把经典模型和深度模型摆在一起比——质量上限、成本、响应时间、好不好排查。
一句用深度学习带过是误解——深度学习可以是候选，但要说明为什么值得。
只谈数据库选型是误解——偏离了模型选择这个问题本身。
optionExplanations_en: Just name-dropping a paper is a misconception — it only convinces if it fits the constraints.
Correct: weigh classic vs. deep families on quality ceiling, price, speed, and debuggability.
Saying "use deep learning" and stopping is a misconception — it needs justification.
Only discussing database choice is a misconception — it sidesteps model selection.

scenario: 你直接提出训练一个超大模型，但数据少、延迟预算紧。
scenario_en: You propose training a very large model, but data is limited and the latency budget is tight.
q: 面试官最可能担心什么？
q_en: What is the interviewer most likely worried about?
options: 担心模型结构太简单、太容易被解释
担心 baseline 已经太强，没必要再建模
过拟合、训练/serving 成本不可行
担心训练标签的获取成本太低
options_en: Worried the model is too simple and too easy to interpret.
Worried the baseline is already too strong to bother modeling further.
Overfitting and infeasible training/serving cost.
Worried the training labels are too cheap to obtain.
why: 复杂模型必须用数据量、质量收益和推理预算支撑，否则显得没有生产经验。
why_en: A large model needs justification through data scale, quality gain, and serving budget.
tradeoff: 模型容量/质量上限 vs 数据量、训练成本、serving 可行性

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型记住训练数据细节，泛化到新数据时表现变差。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Overfitting is when a model memorizes training data details and generalizes poorly to new data.

optionExplanations: 太可解释是误解——可解释性通常降低排查成本，不是风险来源。
baseline 太强是误解——那只说明门槛高，不解释大模型的风险。
对：数据少、延迟紧时，大模型最容易在泛化和 serving 成本上出问题。
标签成本太低是误解——便宜标签通常是优势，场景也没提这个约束。
optionExplanations_en: Being too interpretable is a misconception — that usually lowers debugging cost.
A strong baseline is a misconception — it raises the bar, doesn't explain the risk.
Correct: with little data and tight latency, a large model strains generalization and cost.
Cheap labels being a problem is a misconception — cheap labels are usually a plus.

scenario: 你提出一个双塔排序模型，面试官追问架构细节。
scenario_en: You propose a two-tower ranking model, and the interviewer asks for architecture details.
q: “穿针引线”式回答架构细节是什么意思？
q_en: What does a balanced architecture-detail answer look like?
options: 直接断言“4 层 1024 维一定最优”，不给理由
完全跳过 loss 函数的设计细节不谈
只画云基础设施的部署架构图，不谈模型结构
给出输入、层结构、loss、正则，但不编精确超参
options_en: Flatly claim "4 layers of 1024 is always optimal" with no justification.
Skip explaining the loss function's design details entirely.
Only draw the cloud deployment infrastructure diagram, not the model's internals.
Describe the input, layers, loss, and regularization without inventing exact hyperparameters.
why: 要说明结构关键点，但不假装已知只有实验能定的精确宽度。
why_en: Architecture discussion should be detailed enough to show understanding without pretending empirical hyperparameters are known.

termDefinitions.meaning: 限制模型复杂度以降低过拟合风险的技术，如 dropout、L2。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Regularization limits model complexity to reduce overfitting risk, such as dropout or an L2 penalty.

optionExplanations: 断言某超参必然最优是误解——精确层数和维度要靠实验验证。
跳过 loss 设计是误解——loss 连接训练目标和行为，必须提。
只画云部署图是误解——那答的是 serving 问题，不是模型内部结构。
对：讲清输入、层结构、loss、正则这些关键点，超参留给实验去定。
optionExplanations_en: Flatly claiming one hyperparameter is optimal is a misconception — that needs experiments.
Skipping the loss design is a misconception — it connects the goal to model behavior.
Only drawing the deployment diagram is a misconception — that's serving, not internals.
Correct: cover input, layers, loss, and regularization, and leave exact numbers to experiments.

scenario: 模型训练完成，你要说明如何上线和评估它。
scenario_en: The model is trained, and you need to explain how to serve and evaluate it.
q: Inference and Evaluation 阶段要覆盖哪两类内容？
q_en: What two kinds of topics should inference and evaluation cover?
options: 离线/在线指标，加延迟成本扩展约束
只反复回头检查训练阶段写过的代码
只讨论跟这道题无关的候选人简历背景
只关心产品前端界面的视觉设计细节
options_en: Offline/online metrics plus latency, cost, and scale constraints.
Only repeatedly re-check the code written during the training stage.
Only discuss the candidate's resume background, unrelated to this question.
Only care about the product's frontend visual design details.
why: 应用 ML 成功不仅看模型分数，还要能在 SLA 内服务并改善业务。
why_en: Inference and evaluation cover both metrics and the practical serving constraints such as latency, cost, and scale.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Offline[Offline metrics] --> Gate[Launch gate]
  Online[Online metrics] --> Gate
  Serving[Latency cost scale] --> Gate
  Gate --> Iterate[Iterate]

termDefinitions.meaning: 通过 A/B 实验衡量模型对真实用户业务指标的影响。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Online evaluation measures a model's real impact on business metrics through an A/B experiment.

optionExplanations: 对：一手看指标涨跌，一手看 serving 能不能达标——延迟、成本、扩展都要算进去。
只检查训练代码是误解——那是研发流程，不等于上线评估。
谈候选人简历是误解——跟模型能不能上线完全无关。
只关心前端视觉是误解——除非实验目标本身涉及 UI，否则无关。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: launch decisions need the metric story plus whether serving meets its SLA.
Only re-checking training code is a misconception — that's engineering, not launch evaluation.
Discussing the candidate's resume is a misconception — irrelevant to whether it ships.
Only caring about visuals is a misconception — unrelated unless the experiment targets UI.

scenario: 推荐模型离线 NDCG 提升了，但线上用户留存下降。
scenario_en: A recommender improves offline NDCG, but online user retention drops.
q: 这组结果说明了什么问题？
q_en: What problem do these results reveal?
options: NDCG 的计算公式一定是哪里算错了
离线 ML 指标和业务目标没有完全对齐
留存下降只是噪声，完全可以忽略
指标出现矛盾，模型完全不需要调整
options_en: The NDCG formula must have been computed wrong somewhere.
The offline ML metric and the business objective are not fully aligned.
The retention drop is just noise and can be fully ignored.
Even with conflicting metrics, the model needs no adjustment at all.
why: 离线排序指标只是代理，可能鼓励短期点击而伤害长期满意度。
why_en: A metric gain with worse retention indicates offline ML metrics are not fully aligned with business objectives.
whenOtherWins: 如果留存下降来自无关的外部事件，需要用实验切片排除混杂因素。
tradeoff: 离线代理指标（NDCG） vs 线上业务目标（留存）

termDefinitions.meaning: 衡量排序结果质量、并对靠后位置做折扣的离线指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NDCG is an offline ranking metric that discounts the value of correct results appearing lower in the list.

optionExplanations: 先怀疑计算错误是误解——只有复现出公式或日志错误才该这么归因。
对：离线涨、业务跌，说明这个代理指标和真实业务目标没对齐。
留存下降可以忽略是误解——留存是业务信号，不能被好看的离线分数盖过。
模型不需要调整是误解——指标矛盾时至少要切片分析或重设目标。
optionExplanations_en: Assuming the calculation is wrong is a misconception — only reproduction justifies that.
Correct: offline up and business down means the proxy isn't aligned with the real goal.
Ignoring the retention drop is a misconception — it can't be waved away by an offline win.
Assuming no change is needed is a misconception — contradictory metrics call for slicing.

scenario: 推理阶段的延迟和成本约束很紧，你要挑选优化手段。
scenario_en: Inference latency and cost constraints are tight, and you need to choose optimization techniques.
q: 推理约束紧时可以讨论哪些优化？（多选）
q_en: Which optimizations are worth discussing when inference constraints are tight? (Select all that apply.)
options: 缓存
量化
蒸馏
剪枝
options_en: Caching
Quantization
Distillation
Pruning
why: 这些方法用不同方式降低成本或延迟，但都要以质量回归监控为前提。
why_en: Caching, quantization, distillation, and pruning are common inference optimizations.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把模型权重用更低精度表示以降低计算和内存开销。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Quantization represents model weights with lower precision to cut compute and memory cost.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用一个大模型（teacher）的输出训练一个更小的模型（student）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Distillation trains a smaller student model to mimic a larger teacher model's outputs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 删除模型中冗余的权重或连接以减少计算量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pruning removes redundant weights or connections from a model to reduce computation.

optionExplanations: 缓存命中重复请求，省掉重算，但要防数据变陈旧。
量化降低权重精度，省内存和算力换延迟，但精度掉太多伤质量。
蒸馏用大模型输出训一个小模型，延迟低，但会带上老师模型的偏差。
剪枝砍掉冗余权重减少计算量，但剪过头会让效果明显退化。
optionExplanations_en: Caching absorbs repeat requests and skips recompute, but data can go stale.
Quantization lowers precision to cut memory and compute, trading some accuracy for speed.
Distillation trains a small student on a big teacher's outputs, but inherits teacher bias.
Pruning removes redundant weights to cut compute, but too much pruning regresses quality.

scenario: 你想给一个低 QPS 的离线批处理任务做复杂量化和蒸馏。
scenario_en: You want to apply complex quantization and distillation to a low-QPS offline batch job.
q: 面试里更合理的取舍是什么？
q_en: What is the more reasonable tradeoff in the interview?
options: 默认所有模型上线前都必须做量化处理
直接忽略量化之后的质量回归评估
先确认是否真受推理成本或延迟约束
把这个批处理任务硬改造成实时服务
options_en: Assume every model must be quantized before shipping, by default.
Skip the post-quantization quality-regression evaluation entirely.
Confirm whether cost or latency is actually the constraint.
Force this batch job to be rebuilt as a real-time service.
why: 优化应服务约束，离线低频任务可能更该保质量和可维护性。
why_en: Inference optimizations should be justified by actual latency, cost, or throughput constraints.
whenOtherWins: 若批处理成本巨大或时间窗口很短，量化/蒸馏仍然值得做。
tradeoff: 推理优化收益 vs 额外复杂度和维护成本
optionExplanations: 默认都要量化是误解——低 QPS 场景白背维护成本，收益未必划算。
忽略质量回归是误解——任何有损优化上线前都要检查是否伤了质量。
对：先确认成本或延迟是不是真的紧，再决定要不要加复杂度。
硬改成实时服务是误解——架构该跟着产品需要走，不是反过来迁就优化。
optionExplanations_en: Defaulting to quantization is a misconception — a low-QPS job pays cost for unclear gain.
Skipping quality-regression checks is a misconception — any lossy change needs a check first.
Correct: confirm cost or latency is really the bottleneck before adding complexity to fix it.
Forcing real-time serving is a misconception — architecture follows product need, not the fix.

scenario: 设计进入 Deep Dives 阶段，系统里有冷启动、反馈循环、扩展性等潜在难点。
scenario_en: The design reaches deep dives, and the system has hard parts such as cold start, feedback loops, and scaling.
q: 这一阶段该如何选择要讲的内容？
q_en: How should you choose what to cover in this stage?
options: 不管系统实际难点是什么，都讲自己最熟的强化学习
退回到问题澄清阶段，把流程从头重新开始
回避承认设计里存在任何潜在风险和短板
跟随面试官，或主动列出系统真正的技术难点供选择
options_en: Talk about your favorite reinforcement-learning topic no matter what the system's real hard part is.
Go all the way back and restart the problem-clarification stage from scratch.
Avoid admitting any potential risk or weakness in the design.
Follow the interviewer, or proactively list the design's real hard parts to choose from.
why: 深挖用于展示特定领域深度，要聚焦系统真正的技术难点。
why_en: Deep dives should focus on the most relevant hard parts, either interviewer-driven or clearly offered as options.

termDefinitions.meaning: 新用户或新物品缺乏历史数据，模型难以给出可靠预测的问题。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cold start is the problem of making reliable predictions for new users or items that lack historical data.

optionExplanations: 硬讲自己最熟的话题是误解——不贴合本系统难点，容易跑偏。
退回澄清阶段重来是误解——澄清已完成，该把时间花在具体难点上。
回避任何风险是误解——承认风险并给缓解方案更有说服力。
对：跟着面试官走，或主动把冷启动、反馈循环、扩展性这些难点列出来选。
optionExplanations_en: Forcing your favorite topic is a misconception — it can miss the system's real hard part.
Restarting clarification is a misconception — framing is done, spend time on hard parts now.
Avoiding any admission of risk is a misconception — naming risks with fixes is more convincing.
Correct: follow the interviewer, or offer cold start, feedback loops, scaling as a menu.

scenario: 你在为一个推荐系统列出可深挖的方向。
scenario_en: You are listing possible deep-dive areas for a recommender system.
q: 常见 deep dive 主题包括哪些？（多选）
q_en: What are common deep-dive topics? (Select all that apply.)
options: 冷启动/边界案例
规模与 serving
监控和重训
无关 UI 动画
options_en: Cold start and edge cases
Scaling and serving
Monitoring and retraining
Unrelated UI animations
why: 这些主题直接影响生产可用性和长期质量。
why_en: Common ML design deep dives include cold start, scaling, monitoring, and retraining.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  DeepDive[Deep dive menu] --> Cold[Cold start]
  DeepDive --> Scale[Serving scale]
  DeepDive --> Monitor[Monitor retrain]

termDefinitions.meaning: 线上数据分布随时间变化，导致模型效果衰减。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Model drift is when the live data distribution shifts over time and model performance decays.

optionExplanations: 冷启动/边界案例挡住的是新用户新物品缺数据、模型瞎猜的风险。
规模与 serving 挡住的是上线后 QPS/延迟撑不住的风险。
监控和重训挡住的是模型悄悄漂移、效果衰减却没人发现的风险。
UI 动画跟推荐系统的技术难点无关，是误答案。
optionExplanations_en: Cold start / edge cases block the risk of guessing blind for new users or items.
Scaling and serving block the risk of QPS or latency exceeding what the system handles.
Monitoring and retraining block the risk of the model drifting unnoticed after launch.
UI animation is unrelated to a recommender's technical hard parts.

scenario: 面试官给你一个模糊的系统设计问题，你正要开场。
scenario_en: The interviewer gives you a vague system design prompt, and you are about to start.
q: Problem Framing 阶段的绿旗包括哪些？（多选）
q_en: What are green flags in the problem framing stage? (Select all that apply.)
options: 问到核心约束
建立清晰业务目标
给出可指导后续设计的 ML objective
跳过目标直接报模型
options_en: Asking about the core constraints
Establishing a clear business objective
Giving an ML objective that guides the rest of the design
Skipping the objective and jumping straight to a model
why: 开场要让后续所有选择有依据，跳过目标会暴露约束没对齐。
why_en: Good problem framing clarifies constraints, business objective, and ML objective before modeling.
optionExplanations: 问到核心约束挡住的是设计错方向——规模、延迟不明就动手，容易全盘返工。
建立清晰业务目标挡住的是后续建模没依据、指标全靠拍脑袋的风险。
给出可指导设计的 ML objective 挡住的是数据、模型、评估各说各话的风险。
跳过目标直接报模型是红旗——约束没对齐就先给方案，说明没想清楚。
optionExplanations_en: Asking core constraints blocks the risk of designing in the wrong direction entirely.
A clear business objective blocks the risk of modeling with no basis for its metrics.
An ML objective that guides the design keeps data, modeling, and evaluation from pulling apart.
Skipping the objective for a model is a red flag — constraints were never aligned.

scenario: 你在评估一段 Modeling 阶段的面试表现。
scenario_en: You are evaluating someone's performance in the modeling stage of an interview.
q: Modeling 阶段的红旗包括哪些？（多选）
q_en: What are red flags in the modeling stage? (Select all that apply.)
options: 不考虑 baseline 直接上复杂模型
模型架构完全手挥
不讨论 tradeoff
说明简单基线的作用
options_en: Jumping to a complex model without considering a baseline
Hand-waving the model architecture entirely
Never discussing trade-offs
Explaining what the simple baseline is for
why: 模型讨论要体现实践取舍和理解深度，baseline 本身不是红旗。
why_en: Modeling red flags include skipping baselines, hand-waving architecture, and ignoring tradeoffs.
optionExplanations: 跳过 baseline 直接上复杂模型是红旗——没有地板线，复杂度收益没法验证。
架构完全手挥是红旗——面试官看不出你是否真懂模型内部结构。
不讨论 tradeoff 是红旗——看不到你在约束下做取舍的能力。
说明简单基线的作用不是红旗，反而是加分项——证明你先建了比较地板线。
optionExplanations_en: Skipping the baseline for a complex model is a red flag — there's no floor to prove the gain.
Hand-waving the architecture is a red flag — it hides whether you understand the model.
Never discussing tradeoffs is a red flag — it hides your reasoning under constraints.
Explaining the baseline's role isn't a red flag — it's a plus, showing you built a floor first.

q: 按推荐顺序排列 ML system design delivery framework。
q_en: Put the ML system design delivery framework in the recommended order.
why: 这个顺序先定义问题边界，再讨论数据、模型、上线评估，最后深挖，保证关键评估点都被覆盖。
why_en: The delivery framework moves from framing to high-level design, data, modeling, inference and evaluation, then deep dives.
tradeoff: 覆盖全部关键阶段 vs 在某一阶段停留过久

termDefinitions.meaning: 针对某个具体技术难点进行更细致讨论的阶段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A deep dive is a focused, detailed discussion of one specific hard part of the design.

q: 按正确顺序完成 Problem Framing。
q_en: Put the problem framing steps in the correct order.
why: 先知道问题边界，再定义业务价值，最后把它转成可建模任务。
why_en: Problem framing clarifies scope, establishes the business objective, and then defines the ML objective.
tradeoff: 先约束后目标 vs 先目标后约束

q: 按合理顺序展开 Modeling 讨论。
q_en: Put the modeling discussion steps in a reasonable order.
why: 先建立地板线，再讲选择空间，之后深入并证明复杂度的价值。
why_en: A modeling discussion should start with baselines, compare options, then deep dive and justify complexity.
tradeoff: 先简后繁证明复杂度 vs 一上来就上复杂模型
steps: 比较候选模型家族和 tradeoff
选一个方案深入架构、loss、正则
说明为什么复杂度值得

termDefinitions.meaning: 用来比较后续复杂方案收益的简单参照模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A baseline is a simple reference model used to measure the gain from a more complex approach.

scenario: 你想把业务目标映射到评估指标。
scenario_en: You want to map a business objective into evaluation metrics.
q: 这段伪代码表达了什么思路？
q_en: What idea does this pseudocode express?
codeSample:
business_objective = "reduce harmful views"
product_metric = views_of_harmful_content
ml_metric = recall_at_precision(0.95)
options: 从业务目标逐层派生产品指标和 ML 指标
直接把 ML loss 本身当成业务目标来看待
不管类别是否均衡，只优化 accuracy 一项
为了图省事，直接跳过 precision guardrail
options_en: Derive the product metric and ML metric from the business objective, layer by layer.
Treat the ML loss value itself as the business objective.
Optimize accuracy alone regardless of whether the classes are balanced.
Skip the precision guardrail entirely to save the trouble.
why: 业务目标是减少有害曝光，ML 指标要服从误删 precision guardrail。
why_en: The pseudocode maps a business objective into a product metric and an ML metric with a precision guardrail.
whenOtherWins: 如果业务目标是纯离线研究，产品指标层可能不明显，但仍要说明最终价值。
tradeoff: 从业务目标逐层派生指标 vs 直接把 ML loss 当业务目标
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Biz[Business goal] --> Product[Product metric]
  Product --> ML[ML metric]
  ML --> Guardrail[Guardrail]
  Guardrail --> Decision[Launch decision]

termDefinitions.meaning: 在满足某个精确率门槛的前提下能达到的最高召回率。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Recall at precision is the highest recall achievable while meeting a minimum precision threshold.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给召回类指标设置的最低精确率约束，防止误删过多。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A precision guardrail is a minimum-precision constraint placed on a recall-style metric to prevent excessive false positives.

optionExplanations: 对：代码把业务目标一路收敛成产品指标，再到带精确率门槛的 ML 指标。
把 loss 当业务目标是误解——只有业务层目标缺失时才会这样。
只优化 accuracy 是误解——accuracy 只适合类别均衡、错误代价接近的任务。
跳过 guardrail 是误解——有误删风险时，precision 门槛必须保留。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: the code narrows from business goal to product number to a precision-gated ML metric.
Treating loss as the business objective is a misconception — only happens without a goal layer.
Optimizing accuracy alone is a misconception — that fits balanced, similar-cost classes only.
Skipping the guardrail is a misconception — without it, false positives can run away.

scenario: 推荐系统需要候选生成和排序两个模型，建模只剩 10 分钟，你想把时间花在排序模型上。
scenario_en: Your recommender needs both a candidate generator and a ranker, but only 10 minutes of modeling time remain and you want to spend it on the ranker.
q: 候选生成环节该怎么交代，才不会留下半个系统？
q_en: How should you cover candidate generation so you are not left with half a system?
options: 用热门度排行填上候选生成，一句带过
把候选生成也按双塔召回从头详细展开
直接跳过候选生成，只讲排序模型架构
先把排序模型压成一句话，腾时间讲召回
options_en: Fill candidate generation with a popularity baseline and move on in one sentence.
Also walk through candidate generation as a full two-tower retrieval design.
Skip candidate generation entirely and only describe the ranker architecture.
Compress the ranker into one sentence to free up time for retrieval.
why: baseline 在这里的作用是补位：一句热门度召回就让链路完整，时间留给排序；代价是召回质量没有优化空间，被追问时要主动承认这是占位方案。
why_en: A simple baseline can act as a gap filler so the pipeline is complete, letting you spend the remaining time on the model that actually matters.
whenOtherWins: 若面试官明确说这轮重点是召回，就该反过来：把排序压成 baseline，详细展开候选生成。
tradeoff: 系统链路完整性 vs 单个模型的展开深度

termDefinitions.meaning: 从海量物品里先粗筛出几百个候选，再交给排序模型精排。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Candidate generation narrows millions of items down to a few hundred before the ranker scores them.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户塔和物品塔各自出向量，用向量相似度做大规模召回。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A two-tower model embeds users and items separately and retrieves by vector similarity at scale.

optionExplanations: 对：热门度召回一句就能顶住，链路不缺口，排序模型拿到全部剩余时间。
两个模型都详细展开，10 分钟必然讲不完，排序那块会被腰斩。
跳过召回，面试官会认为你的系统缺了一环，无法评估端到端可行性。
压排序讲召回，除非面试官要求，否则把时间投在了区分度更低的一环。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: a popularity retriever holds the slot in one sentence, leaving all remaining time for the ranker.
Detailing both models cannot fit in 10 minutes and the ranker discussion gets cut short.
Skipping retrieval leaves a visible hole and the interviewer cannot judge end-to-end feasibility.
Compressing the ranker spends your time on the less differentiating half unless asked.

scenario: 新排序模型在留存测试集上 NDCG 比现网高 3%，团队要决定能否全量上线。
scenario_en: A new ranker beats production by 3% NDCG on a held-out test set and the team must decide whether to roll it out.
q: 全量之前必须补哪一步评估？
q_en: Which evaluation step must come before a full rollout?
options: 在更大的历史测试集上重跑离线指标
把离线指标换成 precision@k 再算一遍
跑 A/B 实验，看真实用户的业务指标
让标注团队人工复核一批排序结果
options_en: Re-run the offline metrics on a larger historical test set.
Switch the offline metric to precision@k and recompute.
Run an A/B test and read the real user business metrics.
Have annotators manually review a sample of rankings.
why: 离线评估只是用历史数据估计效果，说不清真实用户行为会怎么变；A/B 才能给出对业务指标的因果结论，代价是要占用线上流量并等一个实验周期。
why_en: Offline metrics only estimate performance from historical data, so you still need an A/B test to see the real business impact.
whenOtherWins: 若推理是小规模离线批处理、没有可分流的实时用户流量，就只能靠离线指标加人工审核决策。
tradeoff: 离线评估的快与便宜 vs 在线 A/B 的因果可信度

termDefinitions.meaning: 归一化折损累积增益：衡量排序结果好坏、且越靠前的位置权重越高的离线指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NDCG, or Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain, scores ranking quality while weighting higher positions more.

termDefinitions.meaning: 推荐的前 k 个结果里，命中用户真实需求的比例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Precision at k is the fraction of the top k recommendations that are actually relevant.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把线上流量随机分成对照组和实验组，比较业务指标差异。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An A/B test splits live traffic randomly between control and treatment to compare business metrics.

optionExplanations: 换更大的历史集只是把同一类估计做得更稳，仍然没有用户行为信息。
换指标改的是离线口径，NDCG 和 precision@k 都读不出留存或转化。
对：只有把真实用户随机分流，才能读出 CTR、转化这类业务指标的变化。
人工复核能抓明显的排序错误，但样本量小，代表不了全量用户反应。
optionExplanations_en: A larger historical set only makes the same estimate steadier; it still carries no user behavior.
Swapping the offline metric changes the yardstick, not the fact that no user reacted to it.
Correct: only randomized live traffic reveals how CTR or conversion actually move.
Manual review catches blatant ranking errors but the sample is too small to represent all users.

scenario: 推荐模型上线三个月后 CTR 缓慢下滑，推理服务没有任何报错，延迟也正常。
scenario_en: Three months after launch the recommender CTR is slowly sliding, yet the inference service throws no errors and latency looks fine.
q: 这种无报错的效果衰减该怎么发现并止损？
q_en: How do you detect and stop a silent quality decay like this?
options: 等用户投诉推荐变差以后再人工排查
给推理服务加更严的 5xx 错误率报警
按固定季度重训一次，不看线上指标
监控 CTR 与多样性，跌破阈值触发重训
options_en: Wait until users complain that recommendations got worse, then investigate.
Add stricter 5xx error-rate alerts on the inference service.
Retrain once a quarter on a fixed cadence without watching live metrics.
Monitor CTR and diversity, and trigger retraining when they cross a threshold.
why: CTR 平稳 → 线上数据分布漂移 → 模型照样返回 200 但排序变差 → 质量指标跌破阈值 → 自动重训并重新上线；代价是重训要吃算力，且每次换模型都带回归风险。
why_en: Drift degrades ranking without any error signal, so you watch quality metrics like CTR and diversity and retrain once they cross a threshold.
whenOtherWins: 若数据分布本身稳定、重训一次的算力成本很高，固定周期重训加人工评审比阈值触发更划算。
tradeoff: 阈值触发重训的时效 vs 重训算力与上线回归风险

termDefinitions.meaning: 线上数据分布随时间偏离训练分布，模型效果悄悄衰减。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Model drift is when live data slowly diverges from the training distribution and quality quietly decays.

termDefinitions.meaning: 点击率：推荐结果被点击的次数除以曝光次数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CTR, or click-through rate, is clicks divided by impressions on the recommendations shown.

termDefinitions.meaning: HTTP 服务端错误状态码，表示服务自身处理失败。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A 5xx status code is an HTTP server-side error meaning the service itself failed to handle the request.

optionExplanations: 等投诉意味着损失已经发生几周，而且多数用户不会投诉，只会少点。
5xx 报警只覆盖服务崩溃，漂移时模型照常返回 200，这条线永远不响。
固定季度重训不看指标，漂移快时来不及，漂移慢时白烧一次算力。
对：把质量指标本身做成报警源，漂移一旦体现在 CTR/多样性上就自动触发重训。
optionExplanations_en: Waiting for complaints means weeks of lost engagement, and most users just click less instead of complaining.
5xx alerts only cover crashes; under drift the model keeps returning 200 so this line never fires.
A fixed quarterly cadence is too slow when drift is fast and wastes compute when it is slow.
Correct: make the quality metric itself the alert source so drift triggers retraining automatically.

scenario: 电商推荐只用协同过滤，信号全部来自用户-物品交互矩阵，而平台每天上架大量新商品。
scenario_en: An e-commerce recommender relies purely on collaborative filtering over the user-item interaction matrix, while new products are listed every day.
q: 纯协同过滤对刚上架的新商品会怎么失效？
q_en: How does pure collaborative filtering break down for a brand-new product?
options: 它会被误判成热门商品而过度曝光，挤掉老商品的位置
没有交互记录 → 不被推荐 → 更拿不到交互
它的交互记录会被错误归并到相似老商品上
矩阵分解会给它随机高分，让推荐噪声变大
options_en: It gets misjudged as a hot item, over-exposed, and crowds established products out of the slots.
No interactions means never recommended, which means it never earns interactions.
Its interactions get misattributed to similar older products.
Matrix factorization gives it a random high score, adding recommendation noise.
why: 协同过滤的全部信号来自历史交互，新商品那一行是空的，于是形成"没曝光→没数据→没曝光"的自锁；破法是补内容特征或对新用户做 epsilon-greedy 探索，代价是探索期要牺牲一部分即时收益。
why_en: Collaborative filtering only sees past interactions, so a new item is an empty row that never gets shown and therefore never earns data.
whenOtherWins: 若目录基本固定、几乎不上新品，纯协同过滤的冷启动缺口可以忽略，不值得引入内容特征的复杂度。
tradeoff: 协同过滤的精度 vs 新物品的可发现性

termDefinitions.meaning: 只根据用户与物品的历史交互模式来推荐，不看物品本身内容。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Collaborative filtering recommends from historical user-item interaction patterns without looking at item content.

termDefinitions.term: content-based filtering / 内容特征推荐
termDefinitions.meaning: 用物品自身属性（标题、类目、图片）匹配用户兴趣，不依赖交互历史。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Content-based filtering matches item attributes such as title, category, or image to user interests without needing interaction history.

termDefinitions.meaning: 大部分时候选当前最优项，以小概率 epsilon 随机探索其他项。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Epsilon-greedy picks the current best option most of the time and explores a random one with a small probability epsilon.

optionExplanations: 过度曝光是误解——新品在矩阵里没有分数，问题恰恰是根本进不了候选。
对：空行→不进候选→拿不到点击→行还是空，自己锁死自己。
归并到老商品是误解——协同过滤按 id 索引交互，不做这种合并。
随机高分是误解——缺失交互通常让分数塌向零，而不是抬高。
optionExplanations_en: Over-exposure is a misconception — a new item has no score at all, so it never enters the candidate set.
Correct: an empty row keeps it out of candidates, so it earns no clicks and the row stays empty.
Misattribution is a misconception — collaborative filtering indexes interactions by item id and does not merge them.
A random high score is a misconception — missing interactions usually collapse the score toward zero.

scenario: Model Selection 环节，你唯一准备的候选方案是今年 NeurIPS 上的一篇新方法。
scenario_en: In model selection, the only candidate you prepared is a brand-new method from this year’s NeurIPS.
q: 只押一篇最新论文会给面试官什么印象？
q_en: What impression does betting on a single brand-new paper leave?
options: 认为你对最近五到七年的研究跟得很紧
怀疑它没有生产验证，稳健性撑不住上线
认为你刻意回避了深度学习这一条路线
认为你把可解释性看得比预测能力更重要
options_en: That you are closely following the research of the last five to seven years.
That it has no production track record and is not robust enough to ship.
That you are deliberately avoiding the deep learning route.
That you value interpretability more than predictive power.
why: 面试官想看的是近两三年经过验证的方法家族：只有一篇今年的论文说明没有生产证据，而只谈五到七年前的方法又会显得知识过时——两头都要避开。
why_en: Interviewers look for approaches proven over the last two or three years, so a single brand-new paper reads as unproven while only old methods read as dated.
whenOtherWins: 若这个岗位本身就是研究型前沿探索岗，提最新论文并讲清它的局限反而是加分项。
tradeoff: 方法的前沿性 vs 生产可验证性

termDefinitions.fullName: Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems
termDefinitions.meaning: 机器学习领域最主要的年度学术会议之一，发表最前沿的研究。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NeurIPS is one of the main annual machine learning research conferences, publishing cutting-edge work.

optionExplanations: 跟得紧是反过来了——单点最新论文恰恰暴露了广度不足。
对：没人在生产里跑过它，面试官无法相信它扛得住线上流量和维护。
回避深度学习不成立——NeurIPS 新方法本身通常就是深度学习路线。
可解释性优先不成立——最新研究方法通常恰恰是最难解释的那一类。
optionExplanations_en: Following closely is backwards — a single new paper actually exposes a lack of breadth.
Correct: nobody has run it in production, so the interviewer cannot trust it under real traffic and maintenance.
Avoiding deep learning does not hold — a new NeurIPS method is usually itself a deep learning approach.
Favoring interpretability does not hold — the newest methods are typically the hardest to interpret.

scenario: ML 设计框架给 High-level Design 的预算是 2-3 分钟，但你已经画了 8 分钟框图，还在调整箭头方向。
scenario_en: The framework budgets 2-3 minutes for high-level design, but you have spent 8 minutes on the block diagram and are still fixing arrows.
q: 框图时间已经超支，接下来该怎么处理？
q_en: You have blown the diagram budget — what should you do next?
options: 停手，用现在的草图直接推进到数据与特征
把框图的组件和箭头补完整再进入数据讨论
删掉框图改成纯口头描述，从头再讲一遍
继续画完，把超支的时间从建模环节里扣掉
options_en: Stop now and move on to data and features with the sketch you already have.
Finish the components and arrows properly before moving to the data discussion.
Delete the diagram, switch to a purely verbal description, and start over.
Finish the drawing and take the overrun out of the modeling section.
why: 2-3 分钟是框架给定的时间预算，不是推导出来的数字；它约束的是框图只当沟通工具用——继续超支就直接吃掉后面 10 分钟数据和 10 分钟建模的深度。
why_en: The 2-3 minute high-level design slot is a given budget, not a derived number, and overrunning it eats straight into the data and modeling depth.
whenOtherWins: 若面试官主动追问组件之间怎么连、数据怎么流，跟随他在框图上多花时间才是对的。
tradeoff: 框图完整度 vs 数据与建模环节的讨论深度

termDefinitions.meaning: 一张展示输入、输出和中间关键组件的框图，用来对齐整体结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A high-level design is a block diagram of inputs, outputs, and the key components between them, used to align on structure.

optionExplanations: 对：草图已经够对齐结构，剩下的评分信号都在数据、建模和评估里。
